summary:
*Abandoned, Not Forgotten — Thrown Away on Purpose is an interactive space documentary and scientific archive built for the NASA Space Apps Challenge. Across our Solar System lie more than 18,000 kilograms of humanity’s greatest robotic explorers—not lost to accidents, but intentionally decommissioned, crashed, or abandoned to protect pristine alien environments and extract sacrificial science until their final transmission.

Our platform transforms verified NASA orbital datasets and Planetary Data System records into an emotional, educational journey across 27 historic missions. Users can explore an interactive 3D Solar System star map, examine detailed 3D spacecraft dossiers with verified telemetry, and test their decision-making in the Director Trials—an ethical simulator putting users in command of high-stakes planetary protection choices. The experience concludes at an interactive 3D Memory Wall paying tribute to human curiosity, supported by an AI Mission Control co-pilot grounded strictly in verified mission facts. 

Every mission leaves something behind; every sacrifice leaves something to remember.
details:
**Abandoned, Not Forgotten — Thrown Away on Purpose** is an interactive space documentary and scientific archive celebrating 27 historic NASA missions left across our Solar System. Across decades of exploration, over 18,000 kilograms of humanity's finest hardware were intentionally de-orbited, crashed, or permanently parked on alien worlds. The platform transforms raw orbital telemetry, disposal logs, and planetary coordinates into an exploratory web application featuring an interactive 3D Solar System map, detailed 3D spacecraft dossiers, an interactive 3D Memory Wall, and an AI Mission Control co-pilot grounded strictly in verified mission records. Central to the platform is the Director Trials—an interactive ethical simulator that puts users in command of high-stakes historical dilemmas, forcing them to balance extra scientific observations against the vital need to de-orbit spacecraft to protect pristine environments like Europa and Enceladus from terrestrial microbes.

By shifting the public narrative of discarded hardware from "space junk" to deliberate scientific and ethical sacrifice, the project bridges dense astrophysics and public engagement. Its intended impact is to demystify planetary protection guidelines established by COSPAR, inspire students and future aerospace engineers, and provide an accessible, open-science educational resource for classrooms and museums worldwide.

The application was developed using TypeScript, React 19, and Vite for a reactive, type-safe architecture, paired with Three.js and WebGL for real-time 3D planetary rendering and spacecraft manipulation. Tailwind CSS v4 and Motion drive the cinematic user interface, while a Node.js and Express backend coordinates data delivery and powers the AI Mission Control via the Google Gemini API. NASA Planetary Data System (PDS) catalogs and JPL mission archives supplied the empirical backbone for all coordinates, mass figures, and citations.

What makes the project uniquely creative is its fusion of rigorous, audited data transparency with emotional documentary storytelling. Rather than acting as a static catalog, it invites active learning through ethical roleplay and an atmospheric, interactive Web Audio soundscape that responds to user input. Throughout development, our team prioritized strict scientific integrity—explicitly flagging dataset nuances and distinguishing confirmed telemetry from working hypotheses—while ensuring universal cross-platform accessibility, smooth performance on consumer devices, and graceful offline fallbacks so the educational experience remains seamless under any network condition.
